summary: Rosina Pastore works in Indology and religious studies. She studied at the University of Naples "L'Orientale", Visva-Bharati University, and the University of Lausanne under Maya Burger and Stefania Cavaliere. She held posts at Lausanne (2016–2022) and Ghent University (2022–2025).
Ross Arthur Leslie Moore was a scholar of Indology and linguistics. He was educated at Dulwich College and Peterhouse, Cambridge, where he later served as Lecturer in Marathi from 1921 to 1927.

Ross Bolleter is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a bachelor's degree at the University of Western Australia under David Tunley. He also studied under John Tarrant and Robert Baker Aitken, and served as a Zen Buddhist teacher (~1991–2023).

Rotem Geva works in history, archaeology, and Indology. She earned an M.A. from The New School and a Ph.D. from Princeton University, later serving as Department Chair at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem in 2016.

Roy Rappaport worked in religious studies and anthropology. He earned his doctorate at Columbia University, chaired the Department of Anthropology at the University of Michigan (~1965–1997), and served as past president of the American Anthropological Association (~1987–1989).

Roy Tzohar specializes in philosophy, Indology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Tel Aviv University under Shlomo Biderman and Columbia University under Gary A. Tubb, Sheldon Pollock, and others, later becoming an associate professor at Tel Aviv University.

Roy W. Perrett is a scholar of philosophy and Indology who studied at the University of Canterbury and the University of Otago. He held posts at Massey University (~1987–2001), the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa, and the University of Melbourne.

Royal W. Weiler was a scholar of Indology and linguistics. He earned his B.A. and Ph.D. at the University of Pennsylvania under W. Norman Brown, later teaching at Columbia University (~1957–1963) and the University of Pennsylvania (~1963–1978).

Royall Tyler is a scholar of Japanology and religious studies who studied at Harvard and Columbia under Donald Keene. He taught at Ohio State, Wisconsin-Madison, Oslo, Harvard, and headed the Japan Centre at Australian National University (1990–2000).
Royce Wiles is an Indologist who completed his Ph.D. at the Australian National University by 2000 and subsequently held a post there.

Rozaliya Osipovna Shor was a linguist and Indologist who studied under Vsevolod Miller. She held posts at RANION, the Institute of Oriental Studies, Baku State University, the Institute for Advanced Training of Teachers, and the Moscow Institute of Philosophy, Literature and History.

Ruben L. F. Habito works in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at Ateneo de Manila, Sophia University, and the University of Tokyo, and held posts at Sophia University, Ryukoku University, Maria Kannon Zen Center, and Southern Methodist University.

Rudi Paret was a scholar of religious studies who studied at the University of Tübingen (~1920–1924). He later held academic posts at the University of Bonn (~1930–1940) and the University of Tübingen (~1941–1968).

Rudolf Carnap was a philosopher who studied at the universities of Jena, Berlin, Freiburg, and Vienna. He held positions at the University of Vienna (1926), Charles University (1931), the University of Chicago (1936–1952), and UCLA (1954).

Rudolf Ernst Wilhelm Meyer was an Indologist and linguist. He studied at Heidelberg University and completed his Ph.D. at Humboldt University of Berlin under Albrecht Weber, also studying under Johannes Schmidt.

Rudolf Fuchs was a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies. He earned his Ph.D. at Humboldt University of Berlin by 1908 under Richard Pischel, also studying under Albrecht Weber, Wilhelm Schulze, and Emil Sieg, among others.
Rudolf Geiger studied at the University of Erlangen-Nuremberg and held a post at the University of Munich from approximately 1937 to 1963.

Rudolf Haym was a scholar of philosophy and history who attended Cöllnisches Gymnasium, Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg, and Berlin. He later held a post at Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg in 1868.

Rudolf Kaschewsky was a scholar of Tibetology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Buddhist studies. Educated at Cologne and Bonn, he taught at Goethe University Frankfurt and served as an Akademischer Oberrat at the University of Bonn (1974–2004).

Rudolf Lange was a scholar in Japanology and linguistics. He held posts at the University of Tokyo from approximately 1874 to 1881 and at Humboldt University of Berlin from approximately 1887 to 1923.
